newsitem.title: UK: Fidelity Brokerage fined $324,000 in Britain.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity Brokerage fined $324,000 in Britain.

text.p: British regulators Thursday fined Fidelity Brokerage Services, the British brokerage arm of Fidelity Investments, 200,000 pounds ($324,000) for breaking rules in settling trades.

Fidelity, which admitted failings in its settlements system, also agreed to pay costs of 162,500 pounds ($270,000), the Securities and Futures Authority said in a statement. The regulatory agency also said it had removed restrictions on Fidelity that have been in place since last October.

The Securities and Futures Authority said Fidelity had experienced problems from converting to a new computer system and an increased volume of business. This led to accounting and reconciliation problems and numerous customer complaints.

"SFA ... is satisfied that the firm now has adequate systems and controls in place to enable it to take on new customers and to introduce new services and ... has restored a satisfactory level of customer service," the authority said.
A Fidelity spokesman said that the SFA acted in an appropriate manner in all its dealings with Fidelity.
"We are very pleased that the SFA has lifted the restrictions on Fidelity Brokerage and that confirms the operational difficulties we had are behind us," spokesman Phil West told Reuters.
West said it would not be appropriate to comment on the size of the fine.
SFA spokesman David Jones said the securities watchdog would "keep close tabs on how they are resuming that business" and Fidelity would be providing regular reports on its progress.

In reaching the settlement, the authority said it had taken into account that investors' money and securities had not been in danger, Fidelity had cooperated fully and the firm had "suffered a significant loss of revenue as a result of the restrictions on new business."
Fidelity had also taken appropriate measures to compensate customers and had devoted significant resources to remedying operational problems and addressing customer concerns, it said.
